Title: August 10, 2023 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session

Topic1.Title: 2023 Midterm Boards and Commissions Appointments
Topic1.Summary: Council held a public hearing on appointments to fill vacancies on the Environmental Advisory Board, Landmarks Board, Open Space Board of Trustees, and University Hill Commercial Area Management Commission. Each vacancy was filled through nominations, alphabetical or reverse-alphabetical voting rounds, and a runoff where needed. Council then approved all selected appointments unanimously by motion. The special meeting was closed and the gavel passed to Council Member Yates for the study session.

Topic2.Title: University Hill Commercial Area Revitalization
Topic2.Summary: Community Vitality staff presented background on the University Hill commercial district, including its General Improvement District, unique liquor and housing regulations, safety concerns, high commercial vacancy, and funding limitations. Staff summarized Urban Land Institute technical advisory panel recommendations, including broad district-wide strategies focused on identity, connectivity, and activation. Staff also outlined longer-term options for the 14th Street parking lot, such as a sale or lease, a parking garage, or mixed-use development. Council generally supported prioritizing broad strategies, exploring code changes such as the liquor and 50/50 food sales rules, and continuing engagement with the University Hill Commercial Area Management Commission and community stakeholders.

Topic3.Title: Affordable Commercial Pilot Program
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented the high cost of commercial space in Boulder, including triple net leases, rising retail rates, and the existing city affordable commercial efforts. A CU Boulder MBA student team presented its proposed pilot program, which would sublease city-leased space to small businesses and nonprofits and provide free education and training. Staff recommended partnering with a community organization, conducting broad community engagement, and using available ARPA and Central Area General Improvement District funds. Council expressed general support for developing the pilot while raising questions about cost, long-term funding sustainability, eligibility criteria, and how to measure success.
